solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Useless male welcoming lives being a fop?

indicators.note: a host welcoming guests takes them inside, so the words before it take in what follows

blocks.note: a dud is something that does not work
standard abbreviation for male
'lives' in the sense 'exists', the verb 'is'

explanation.surface: A worthless man who lives only to dress up, a dandy through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welcoming' makes the useless male a single host around 'lives'; a dude was originally a dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dude is an old word for a dandy, so the state or behaviour of a dude is foppishness.

clue.text: Annoyed with rejection of excuse treated with contempt

indicators.note: rejection throws something out, so the excuse's letters are thrown out of the first word

blocks.note: annoyed, put out
a plea is an excuse offered

explanation.surface: Someone was irritated when their excuse was dismissed out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Take PLEA out of DISPLEASED and DISSED is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To diss is slang for to disrespect or insult, so dissed means scorned or slighted.

clue.text: Straighten end off hook right and left

indicators.note: with its end off, the word for hook loses its final letter

blocks.note: uncus is the anatomical and botanical term for a hook-shaped part
standard abbreviation for right
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Instructions for bending a hook straight, with its tip snipped and working right and left.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCUS is Latin for hook, kept in Chambers; dock its S and add R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncurl something is to unroll it from a coiled shape so that it lies straight.

clue.text: A clique involved in reverse of occasional bravado

indicators.note: being involved in something means sitting inside it, so the clique goes inside the next part
the reverse of a word is that word read from its last letter back to its first

blocks.note: taken as written
a ring is a tight group of conspirators
as in 'the odd visit', meaning occasional

explanation.surface: A small group gets mixed up in an act of only occasional bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd means occasional as in 'the odd visit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do, of which this is a variant spelling, is reckless daring, a showy brand of courage.

clue.text: Bird in South Africa displays such bones

indicators.note: one thing in another is held inside it, so the bird sits within the country

blocks.note: a tern is a seabird
standard abbreviation for South Africa

explanation.surface: A bird in South Africa shows off a skeleton of a particular kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Such' points back to the bird: a bird's breastbone is its sternum, and the plural is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterna is the Latin plural of sternum, the breastbone, which in birds forms a large keel.

clue.text: Strong alloy in mass one with mallet hammered (10, two words)

indicators.note: something hammered is beaten out of shape, so its letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: M is the symbol for mass
taken as written
the letters of mallet rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough metal being beaten with a mallet in a forge.
explanation.walkthrough: MONEL METAL is a hard-wearing nickel-copper alloy; M and ONE come first, then the mallet letters reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Monel metal is a corrosion-resistant nickel and copper alloy prized for its toughness.

clue.text: Poem rewritten, publicity that's recalled large shops

indicators.note: rewriting a piece can rearrange it, so the word poem has its letters reordered
recalled means called back, so the word for publicity runs backwards

blocks.note: the four letters of poem rearranged
to give something air is to give it publicity

explanation.surface: An advertising jingle is rewritten and a campaign withdrawn for department stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poem rewritten' looks like the whole clue's subject; it is just the opening shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is the Latin plural of emporium, a big store or trading centre selling many goods.

clue.text: Regularly deflates young in sty?

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Something keeps going down, perhaps the piglets lying in their pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An elt is a dialect word for a young sow, so elts are young pigs found in a sty.

clue.text: Rooster may command this element of supercharge

indicators.note: an element is one part of a whole, so the letters are a part found inside the next word

blocks.note: the letters are found inside, after the first two

explanation.surface: A cockerel lords it over the yard from some vantage point, amid a supercharged atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: A rooster here is anything that roosts, and it 'rules the roost' from its high spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that roosts sits on a raised bar or branch, and from there it commands the view.

clue.text: Nouns maybe contributing to lingo, a thousand

indicators.note: the words contribute letters to the result, so the answer spans the following words

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word, the a, and the start of the last word

explanation.surface: A grammar point about how nouns contribute to a language of thousands of words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nouns' is not the part of speech: it is an archaic exclamation, short for 'God's wounds', like zounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Old curses such as 'nouns' and 'zounds' were mild swearing exclamations, examples of a profanity.

clue.text: Colicky condition got from fungal cap, not the first

indicators.note: not the first means without its opening letter, which is dropped

blocks.note: pileus is the botanical term for a mushroom's cap

explanation.surface: Stomach cramps caught from eating a bad mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Behead PILEUS to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ileus is an obstruction of the intestine, causing severe colicky abdominal pain.

clue.text: Afternoon fling turning up to get drunk

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: as in a.m. and p.m., a is short for afternoon in Chambers
to toss is to fling

explanation.surface: An afternoon affair that leads to getting tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' looks like a romance, but it is a verb, to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Assot is a Spenserian word meaning befooled or besotted, and besotted can mean stupefied by drink.

clue.text: Unfit, I note? Then one has something to deal with that

blocks.note: taken as written
n. is the abbreviation for a note, as in a footnote reference
a is one, the indefinite article
physical training is the remedy for being out of shape

explanation.surface: Noticing that you are out of shape, you take up exercise to fix it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads naturally about physical unfitness; PT, physical training, deals with that.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or not appropriate for the purpose, much as unfit can.

clue.text: Hen in parlour sat fidgeting

indicators.note: fidgeting means restless movement, so these letters shift around

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A chicken that got into the front room sat there restlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australorp is an Australian breed of domestic chicken developed from Orpingtons, so it is a hen.

clue.text: Noblemen in jewels doffing cap

indicators.note: doffing a cap takes off what is on top, so the first letter is removed

blocks.note: pearls are jewels

explanation.surface: Aristocrats wearing their finest gems take off their hats.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the P from PEARLS.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking below a marquess, so earls are members of the nobility.

clue.text: Enter clusters scribbled – they're graphically simulated (13, two words)

indicators.note: scribbling scrawls letters out of order, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Instructions to type in some groups, hastily jotted, for a computer drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: Screen turtles are the on-screen cursors of Logo-style drawing programs, modelled on the floor-crawling turtle robots.
explanation.definitionFit: In computer graphics a screen turtle is a pointer that imitates a physical drawing robot on the display.

clue.text: She pursues would-be partner of herself, plaited hair trailing

indicators.note: trailing means following behind, so the hair comes after the first piece

blocks.note: sui is Latin for of himself or of herself
a tress is a lock or plait of hair

explanation.surface: A woman chasing a man, her braid flowing behind her.
explanation.walkthrough: SUI is the Latin genitive reflexive, as in sui generis, 'of its own kind'.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitress is a woman who woos or courts someone, the female counterpart of a suitor.

clue.text: Distracted centre if dodging

indicators.note: dodging means darting about, so the letters move into a different order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A flustered player weaving about in the middle of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic originally meant mad or frenzied, and being driven to distraction is a near equivalent.

clue.text: Feel tenderness, as poet did? It's in the heart thereof

indicators.note: thereof points back to the earlier word, and its heart is its centre, where the letters sit

blocks.note: letters five to eight of the word

explanation.surface: A question about how the poets felt affection, answered by looking at its core.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue word doubles as definition and hiding place; 'thereof' sends you back to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Erne, or earn, is a Spenserian verb meaning to yearn or grieve, a feeling of longing and pity.

clue.text: A T-shirt flapping about becomes so dry

indicators.note: a garment flapping about is tossed in all directions, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A T-shirt hung on the line flaps in the wind until it is dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like the laundry drying, but it means thirsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Athirst means thirsty, and someone with a dry throat is said to be dry.

clue.text: To make romantic love (in Rome) I'll get caught in entwining of legs

indicators.note: being caught in something means ending up held inside it
entwined things are twisted together, so the limbs' letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: the letters of legs in a new order
amor is Latin for love
read as 'I will', with I as the subject who gets caught

explanation.surface: A tangle of limbs on a Roman holiday, the stuff of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To make romantic love' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'romantic'; 'love (in Rome)' asks for the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: To glamorise something is to make it appear more attractive or exciting than it is.

clue.text: One working on board in club raised second note

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means lifted upward, so the note is read from the bottom

blocks.note: an iron is a golf club
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A club member promoted to the board, second in line for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a company board; it is an ironing board.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who presses clothes stands over an ironing board while working.

clue.text: Bad fall in the night? Catch one deprived of oxygen

indicators.note: deprived of means having something taken away, so a letter goes

blocks.note: sere, or sear, is the catch in a gunlock
taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Someone takes a nasty tumble in the dark and needs catching, gasping for air.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from ONE and add NE to SERE. 'Fall' is not a tumble but something falling from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene is an old word for a fine rain or damp dew falling after sunset, thought harmful to health.

clue.text: Scotsman's chairman putting energy into journalism

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside

blocks.note: the press is journalism collectively
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Scottish committee head bringing new vigour to the newspaper trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Preses is a Scots term, from Latin, for a president or chairman of a meeting.

clue.text: Old angler having roll round depth

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the list wraps the other letter

blocks.note: a roll is a list of names, a roster
standard abbreviation for depth

explanation.surface: A veteran fisherman checks the register before plumbing the water's depth.
explanation.walkthrough: D sits inside ROSTER, after ROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodster is an archaic word for a fisherman, one who uses a rod and line.

clue.text: Such as standard ramblers

blocks.note: surface reading: ordinary hikers, typical walkers in the countryside
setter's reading: 'standard' and 'rambler' are both kinds of a garden flowering shrub

explanation.walkthrough: A standard is a shrub trained on a single upright stem; ramblers are climbers with long flexible canes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners grow these flowering shrubs both as standards and as climbing ramblers, two familiar forms.

clue.text: What turns to seed, almost past containing centre of culm

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
the centre of a word is its middle letters, which alone are kept
containing means holding inside, so the shortened word wraps the middle letters

blocks.note: over means finished, past
the middle two letters

explanation.surface: Something nearly over, going to seed, with a grass stem at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: A culm is the jointed stem of a grass or sedge.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is the structure in a plant's ovary which develops into a seed after fertilisation.

clue.text: Wee Catherine, Gaelic style, centre of cortege trailing

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, which is the one taken out to move
trailing means following behind, so the lifted letter goes at the end

blocks.note: a cortege is a train of followers or mourners

explanation.surface: A little girl in Scotland walks at the back of a funeral procession.
explanation.walkthrough: Lift the middle A out of TRAIN and let it trail at the end. Trina is a Scottish pet form of Catherine.
explanation.definitionFit: Trina is a diminutive of Catriona, the Gaelic form of Catherine, so it is a Scottish pet name.

clue.text: Gutter for Jock, first to last? That's wallop for you

indicators.note: moving the first letter to the end rotates the word round by one place

blocks.note: rone is Scots for a gutter or drainpipe

explanation.surface: A Scotsman sent sprawling into the gutter by a good thump.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock means Scottish usage. Shift R from the front of RONE to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A oner is a single heavy blow, a knockout punch that does the job in one go.

clue.text: Old cow? Pat mounts under one

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means climbing upward, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: a is one
a pat of butter is a small lump, a wad

explanation.surface: An elderly cow, with a farmhand climbing on to stroke it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is not the animal but a verb, to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaw is a Spenserian word meaning to daunt or subdue, much as cowing someone does.

clue.text: Dry measure in set? It protects against chromosomal deterioration

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a tele is a television set
an omer is a Hebrew dry measure

explanation.surface: A measure dried in a mould, a lab technique to stop genes decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: The omer is a Hebrew dry measure from the Bible, and a tele is short for a television set.
explanation.definitionFit: A telomere is the cap at each end of a chromosome which stops it fraying during cell division.

clue.text: Mild expletive to render en clair, without extremes

indicators.note: with no extremes, the word loses its outermost letters at both ends

blocks.note: en clair means in plain language, so to render it so is to decode

explanation.surface: A gentle curse at having to translate a secret message into plain text.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip D and E from the ends of DECODE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecod is an old exclamation, a minced oath like egad, used as a mild curse.

clue.text: I count beads as transferred in junior church offices

indicators.note: transferred means moved about, so the letters are shifted into new places

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cleric telling the rosary while moved between minor posts in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A subdiaconate is the rank or office of subdeacon, a minor order beneath deacon in the church.

clue.text: Rock consisting of panache, fitted with volume

indicators.note: something fitted with an extra part has it set into it

blocks.note: élan is flair, dash
standard abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: Rock music played with flair and turned up loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music; it is a stone, and elvan is a Cornish quarrymen's name for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvan is a Cornish name for a quartz-porphyry, a hard igneous stone found in dykes.

clue.text: Feature of spore, section thrice stripped from libido

indicators.note: stripped from means taken away, and thrice means three times over

blocks.note: sexiness is sexual appeal or drive
s. is the abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: A biology class covers one part of a spore, then three chapters on sex drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Take all three S's out of SEXINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The exine is the tough outer coat of a pollen grain or spore, a characteristic part of its structure.

clue.text: Heading for the deep drainage channel in green turf

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: sward is an expanse of short grass
ea is a dialect word for a river or drainage channel in the Fens

explanation.surface: A ditch running through the lawn carries water towards the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Ea is a Fenland word for a river or drain, found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaward means towards the sea, and the deep is a poetic name for the ocean.

clue.text: Priest mostly withdrawing for time of worship

indicators.note: mostly means all but a bit, so the final letter is lost

blocks.note: P is an abbreviation for priest
a recess is a withdrawing or retirement

explanation.surface: The vicar almost retires from service at the hour of prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: RECESS loses its last S after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Preces are the versicles and responses said in church services, the prayers at a set hour of devotion.
